Images.Description: C5aR1+/CD11b+ cells correspond to immunosuppressive TAMs

Header: The observed C5aR1+/CD11b+ cells were identified as tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), consistent with their myeloid phenotype and with previous single-nucleus RNA-seq data showing that C5AR1 and ITGAM/ITGB2 (CD11b + CD18, composing the receptor to iC3b, CR3) co-expression is particularly enriched in TAMs.

Waypoints.Name: C5aR1+/CD11b+ macrophages
Waypoints.Description: The release of anaphylatoxins such as C3a and C5a, which act as chemoattractants, correlates with immune cell recruitment to the tumor site. Complement responsive macrophages (C5aR+/CD11b+/CD68+) accumulate in close proximity to C3+/CA9+ malignant cells.

Waypoints.Name: C5aR1+/CD11b+ macrophages and T cells
Waypoints.Description: C5aR1+/CD11b+ macrophages exhibited a C1qTAM phenotype, characterized by C1q and MHC-II expression, and were found in close proximity to CTLA4+ T cells. Their expression of PD-L1 suggests a role in modulating local T-cell responses. Overall, the local production C1q by TAMs initiates the CP activation within the TME, leading to the recruitment of immune cells via C5a. Together with their close spatial association with T cells, these C1qTAMs contribute to the establishment of an immunosuppressive microenvironment that dampens local T-cell responses.
